messages.subject_clean: Bioc-teaching meeting: Monday 9 November at 2pm CET
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

just a reminder that the next Bioconductor teaching call will take place on Monday, November 9 at 2pm CET. The plan for this time is to discuss what properties we would need from a data set that could ideally be used throughout the intro module, and how/where we can find such a data set. Thus, we’d encourage everyone to give some thought to the types of figures/analyses that we would like to include in the module (based on the high-level objectives that we worked on previously), and what we would need from the data in order to achieve this goal.

The jitsi link is the usual one: https://meet.jit.si/BioconductorTeaching

See you on Monday,
Charlotte & Laurent

messages.subject: EuroBioc abstract
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

As agreed during the Bioconductor teaching call yesterday, I started assembling a short abstract for the EuroBioc conference. You can find it here: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1J3OAGauhy4CwDvOkZke2X3E4jjufRAxeTcuqMvmTVO8/edit?usp=sharing (I’ve added the link also to the regular Google Doc). Please have a look and suggest any edits in there, at your earliest convenience but latest on Sunday (Nov 15), so that it can be submitted before the deadline. As a reminder, we are submitting this for a short talk (8 min).

Thanks!
Charlotte

messages.subject: Example plots for Bioc teaching
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I've started generating a few plots following the notes of the meeting, and storing them in a separate Google doc, to avoid overloading the main one.
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Pe0EKQAGkT2-FpYdNAxbgYkaW-LhU3YFHVIpM3exVJo/edit?usp=sharing

I'm also storing the code that I've used at https://github.com/kevinrue/bioc-teaching-intro for full reproducibility. (I've hit a timeout using GEOquery where I've had to run a few Shell commands manually, but I've included those in a Shell script in the repo too).

In the notes of the meeting, "Lines showing expression of genes over time." makes total sense, but is slightly complicated for single cell, as individual cells were not tracked over time.
At best I can draw a smooth trend. Have a look at the plots and you'll see what I mean.

One more thing: I only plot counts on a log axis, to avoid any transformation of the data at this point, which means it's not properly normalised. I understood that for the purpose of an introduction lesson, that's what people would be working with.

Happy to hear feedback any time.
I'll kick that along as I get the chance.

Best
Kevin

messages.subject: RE: EuroBioc abstract
messages.body_plain:
I love group editing! I didn’t have any ideas for the abstract at first, but then after Robert put in his suggestions, I felt there were some needed connections between the Carpentries project and why we had the goals we did. I added few sentences on instructor training and current R modules, but I’m not super happy with my wording so please improve if you can.

Jenny
